question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s centralized authority as CCP General Secretary, sustained through repeated anti-corruption purges that sidelined potential rivals in the Politburo and military, drives the 95.5% trader consensus against removal before 2027. Prior norms of generational turnover were already set aside after his third term, and the 21st Party Congress scheduled for late 2027 is viewed as the likely setting for a fourth term rather than transition, given the absence of a designated successor and ongoing public appearances plus policy continuity through mid-2026. Low-probability scenarios that could still alter outcomes include sudden health events, major economic disruptions prompting elite fractures, or unexpected institutional challenges within the party apparatus before year-end 2026.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democratic Party sources.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination remains wide open more than two years before the primaries, with prediction markets assigning Newsom, Ossoff, and Ocasio-Cortez the clearest early edges due to name recognition, fundraising potential, and positioning within a party still recalibrating after 2024. No major candidates have declared, keeping the field fluid and probabilities clustered near the top. Recent catalysts include the Democratic National Committee's July 2026 approval of a new primary calendar starting in South Carolina and extending through Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia, which broadens geographic and demographic testing grounds. Ossoff has gained ground in trader pricing amid strong reelection positioning in Georgia, while AOC secured her House nomination and posted competitive early poll numbers in New Hampshire. Harris retains residual visibility but trails the leaders. Separation is likely to emerge from 2026 midterm outcomes, formal announcements, major fundraising reports, or shifts in national polling that highlight electability against a Republican incumbent.
